title: Canonical enriched-hammock comparison for simplicial sets and Kan complexes
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, internal functor simplicial sets, Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], simplicial categories and Dwyer--Kan equivalences of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and the diagonal reduced hammock category $\operatorname{diag}H(A,U)$ of [def-coef-simplicial-hammock-pair]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ and enlarge the ambient universes so that all the categories below are small. Let $\mathcal S_*$ be the simplicial category of all $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets, with mapping object $\mathcal S_*(A,B)=\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)$, composition induced by evaluation, and identity the constant identity map. Let $\mathcal K_*$ be its full simplicial subcategory of Kan complexes, and $\mathcal S_0,\mathcal K_0$ their ordinary categories of vertices. For an ordinary category $P$, write $P^{\mathrm{disc}}$ for the simplicial category with the same objects and the constant simplicial sets on the sets $P(x,y)$ as mapping objects, with composition and identities those of $P$. Let $W\subseteq\mathcal S_0$ be the wide subcategory of weak homotopy equivalences and put $W_{\mathcal K}=W\cap\mathcal K_0$.

View $W$ as the wide simplicial subcategory $W^{\mathrm{disc}}\subseteq\mathcal S_*$ whose degree-$r$ arrows are the constant maps $A\times\Delta^r\to B$ induced by maps $A\to B$ in $W$, with identity simplicial operators; similarly define $W_{\mathcal K}^{\mathrm{disc}}$. Set
$$H_{\mathcal S}=\operatorname{diag}H(\mathcal S_*,W^{\mathrm{disc}}),\qquad H_{\mathcal K}=\operatorname{diag}H(\mathcal K_*,W_{\mathcal K}^{\mathrm{disc}}),\qquad H_0=\operatorname{diag}H(\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{disc}},W^{\mathrm{disc}}).$$
In $H_0$, $W^{\mathrm{disc}}$ denotes the wide simplicial subcategory $W^{\mathrm{disc}}\subseteq\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{disc}}$ with the constant mapping simplicial sets on the sets $W(A,B)$. Thus $H_0$ is the ordinary reduced hammock localization of $(\mathcal S_0,W)$, retaining the hammock simplicial direction. There are canonical simplicial functors
$$\mathcal K_*\xrightarrow{b}H_{\mathcal K}\xrightarrow{j}H_{\mathcal S}\xleftarrow{a}H_0.$$
Here $b$ sends a degree-$r$ arrow to the width-$r$ one-arrow hammock with that arrow repeated in all rows and identity vertical arrows, followed by reduction; $j$ applies the full inclusion of Kan complexes to every hammock arrow; and $a$ replaces each ordinary arrow in a width-$r$ hammock by its constant degree-$r$ simplex. Each of $a,b,j$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Write $h:\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{disc}}\to H_0$ for the one-arrow hammock functor, $i:\mathcal K_0^{\mathrm{disc}}\to\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{disc}}$ for inclusion, and $v:\mathcal K_0^{\mathrm{disc}}\to\mathcal K_*$ for the vertex-category functor. The square commutes as simplicial functors:
$$a\circ h\circ i=j\circ b\circ v.$$
These are assertions about the specified enriched functors, including their compositions and identities, rather than only pairwise equivalences of mapping spaces.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Function complexes in homotopical algebra, Proposition 4.8 and its commutative diagram, printed pp.432-433, specialized to the Kan model category of simplicial sets; proof with functorial factorizations in Section 7.4, p.437. Also Hinich, Dwyer--Kan localization revisited, Proposition 1.3.5, p.7. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this enriched-hammock comparison.

proof.text: The formulas for $a,b,j$ define simplicial functors. Indeed applying an operator to a one-arrow diagram gives the one-arrow diagram of that operator; deleting or repeating rows of a repeated-arrow diagram gives the repeated-arrow diagram with the new number of rows. Constant simplices commute with all operators. Applying inclusion or taking constants commutes with composing adjacent columns and deleting identity columns. Concatenating two one-arrow diagrams and reducing composes their arrows; the identity arrow reduces to the empty path. These observations, using [def-coef-simplicial-hammock-pair], prove all functor and operator identities, including the case of identity arrows. On a degree-$r$ arrow of $\mathcal K_0^{\mathrm{disc}}$, both $ahi$ and $jbv$ are the same constant arrow repeated in the same $r+1$ rows, with identity vertical maps; their reductions are identical. Thus the asserted square commutes strictly.

source.place: Proposition 4.8, pp.432-433; agent-written specialization and explicit functorial argument, using the existing localization interfaces rather than assuming that pairwise mapping-space identifications preserve composition.

proof.text: For every simplicial set $X$ and $k\geq0$, projection $\pi_X:X\times\Delta^k\to X$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The section at vertex $0$ is a right inverse. The monotone map $[k]\times[1]\to[k]$ sending $(u,0)$ to $0$ and $(u,1)$ to $u$ induces a simplicial homotopy between the section followed by projection and the identity of $X\times\Delta^k$, fixing the $X$ coordinate. [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] realizes this as a continuous homotopy, and [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak] proves the assertion, without nonemptiness or Kan assumptions. If $w:X\to Y$ is weak, the equality $\pi_Y(w\times1)=w\pi_X$ and two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] show that $w\times1_{\Delta^k}$ is weak as well.

source.place: Proposition 4.8, pp.432-433; agent-written specialization and explicit functorial argument, using the existing localization interfaces rather than assuming that pairwise mapping-space identifications preserve composition.

proof.text:
Fix $k$. Write $C_k=(\mathcal S_*)_k$ for the ordinary category with maps $f:X\times\Delta^k\to Y$ and composition $(g\star f)(x,t)=g(f(x,t),t)$. Its marked arrows are just constant simplices of $W$. Define $c_k:\mathcal S_0\to C_k$ by constants, and $T_k:C_k\to\mathcal S_0$ by
$$T_kX=X\times\Delta^k,\qquad (T_kf)(x,t)=(f(x,t),t).$$
The displayed composition formula proves that $T_k$ is a functor, including identities. By Step 2 it preserves marked arrows; so does $c_k$. There is an ordinary natural transformation $\pi:T_kc_k\to1_{\mathcal S_0}$ consisting of projections, all in $W$. There is also a natural transformation $e:1_{C_k}\to c_kT_k$ whose component is the $k$-arrow $e_X(x,t)=(x,t)$. Naturality is the equality $(f(x,t),t)=(f(x,t),t)$. The constant $k$-arrow $c_k(\pi_X)$ is marked and satisfies $c_k(\pi_X)\star e_X=1_X$. We do not assert that $e_X$ itself is a constant marked arrow.

source.place: Proposition 4.8, pp.432-433; agent-written specialization and explicit functorial argument, using the existing localization interfaces rather than assuming that pairwise mapping-space identifications preserve composition.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] to the two ordinary relative categories of Step 3. The relative functors $c_k,T_k$ induce functors between their coherent localizations. The transformation $\pi$ becomes a natural equivalence. Each $e_X$ also becomes an equivalence: $q(c_k\pi_X)$ is invertible and its composite with $q(e_X)$ is the identity, so the class of $q(e_X)$ in the homotopy category is its inverse; [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] detects equivalence edges by these classes. By the component criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $q(e)$ is a natural equivalence. The full faithfulness on coherent functor categories in the localization universal property descends both transformations, and reflects their being equivalences. Thus the two induced composites are equivalent to the identity, proving that the induced $c_k$ is a functor equivalence. By the mapping-space clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the actual hammock map
$$H(\mathcal S_0,W)(X,Y)\longrightarrow H(C_k,W^{\mathrm{disc}}_k)(X,Y)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $X,Y$: the natural coherent-nerve comparisons of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identify its Kan replacements with the induced mapping-space maps. No assertion that $C_k$ is a model category is used.

source.place: Proposition 4.8, pp.432-433; agent-written specialization and explicit functorial argument, using the existing localization interfaces rather than assuming that pairwise mapping-space identifications preserve composition.

proof.text: For fixed $X,Y$, the source of the comparison in Step 4 is constant in $k$ and the target forms the bisimplicial set $H((\mathcal S_*)_k,W^{\mathrm{disc}}_k)(X,Y)_r$. The maps $c_k$ commute with all operators in $k$ because constant simplices do; no naturality in $k$ of the auxiliary $T_k$ is needed. Step 4 gives weak equivalences in the $r$ direction for each $k$. [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] therefore gives a weak equivalence on diagonals. Its degree-$n$ formula is exactly $a$: replace every ordinary arrow in a width-$n$ hammock by its constant $n$-simplex. By [def-coef-simplicial-hammock-pair] these are its source and target mapping sets. As $a$ fixes all objects, local weak equivalence also gives an equivalence of component categories; hence $a$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 4.8, pp.432-433; agent-written specialization and explicit functorial argument, using the existing localization interfaces rather than assuming that pairwise mapping-space identifications preserve composition.

proof.text:
Let $P=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$ with unit $\eta$ as in [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products]. Its product comparisons give it a simplicial enrichment: on a parameterized map $f:X\times\Delta^k\to Y$ use
$$PX\times\Delta^k\xrightarrow{1\times\eta_{\Delta^k}}PX\times P\Delta^k\xrightarrow{\cong}P(X\times\Delta^k)\xrightarrow{Pf}PY.$$
This formula commutes with every simplicial operator by naturality of $\eta$. For $g\star f$, the product projections give the formula $Pg(Pf(x,\eta(t)),\eta(t))$; it is the composite of the displayed maps for $f,g$, since $P$ carries the diagonal of the parameter to its diagonal and $\eta$ commutes with the two projections. Identity maps give projection onto $PX$. Thus this is a simplicial functor $P:\mathcal S_*\to\mathcal K_*$. Naturality of $\eta$ applied to $f$, together with its compatibility with products, says that $\eta_Y f=P(f)(\eta_X\times1)$ as parameterized maps. This is enriched naturality, not merely naturality on vertices. The same node says $PX$ is Kan and $\eta_X$ is weak. If $w$ is weak then $Pw$ is weak by $Pw\eta_X=\eta_Yw$ and two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. In particular $P$ maps every constant marked arrow to a constant marked arrow, and restricts to $\mathcal K_*$ as well.

source.place: Proposition 4.8, pp.432-433; agent-written specialization and explicit functorial argument, using the existing localization interfaces rather than assuming that pairwise mapping-space identifications preserve composition.

proof.text: In degree $k$ let $J_k:(\mathcal K_*)_k\to(\mathcal S_*)_k$ be inclusion and use $P_k$ of Step 6 in the other direction. They preserve the constant marked subcategories. The enriched natural unit restricts to ordinary natural transformations $1\to J_kP_k$ and $1\to P_kJ_k$ with components the constant $k$-simplices of $\eta_X$, which are marked weak arrows. Write $q_S,q_K$ for the two localization functors. By [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization], $J_k$ and $P_k$ induce functors $\bar J_k,\bar P_k$ between the coherent localizations. Composing the two unit transformations with $q_S,q_K$ gives transformations $q_S\to\bar J_k\bar P_kq_S$ and $q_K\to\bar P_k\bar J_kq_K$. Their components are equivalences since localization inverts every marked arrow. The component criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes both transformations equivalences. The full faithful restriction on functor categories in the localization universal property lifts them to natural equivalences $1\simeq\bar J_k\bar P_k$ and $1\simeq\bar P_k\bar J_k$. Thus $\bar J_k$ and $\bar P_k$ are inverse functor equivalences. Its natural mapping comparisons and [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] show that $H(J_k)$ induces a weak equivalence on every mapping simplicial set between Kan endpoints. Applying [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] over $k$ yields local weak equivalences for the specified $j$. Every object $X$ of $H_{\mathcal S}$ is isomorphic in its component category to $PX$, an object in the image of $j$: the forward one-arrow hammock of $\eta_X$ and the backward one-arrow hammock are inverse there, the cancellation relations being the two-row hammocks with vertical arrow $\eta_X$ (all ordinary arrows embedded as constants). This uses only the defining row operations of [def-coef-simplicial-hammock-pair]. Thus $j$ is essentially surjective as well, and is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 4.8, pp.432-433; agent-written specialization and explicit functorial argument, using the existing localization interfaces rather than assuming that pairwise mapping-space identifications preserve composition.

proof.text: Every weak equivalence $w:A\to B$ of Kan complexes is invertible in $\pi_0\mathcal K_*$. Indeed [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance], with target $A$, gives a bijection on components for $w^*:\operatorname{Fun}(B,A)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,A)$. Choose a vertex $g:B\to A$ mapping to the identity component, so $gw$ lies in that component. With target $B$, injectivity on components for $w^*$ implies $wg$ is in the identity component: its precomposition with $w$ has component $wgw=w$, the same as that of $1_B$. Composition respects components because enriched composition is a simplicial map. This supplies both inverse equations in the component category of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], including empty complexes; no Whitehead theorem or unproved composition compatibility is inferred.

source.place: Proposition 4.8, pp.432-433; agent-written specialization and explicit functorial argument, using the existing localization interfaces rather than assuming that pairwise mapping-space identifications preserve composition.

proof.text: Let $I\subseteq\mathcal K_*$ have only the identity simplex at each diagonal mapping set and empty off-diagonal mapping sets, and let $V=W_{\mathcal K}^{\mathrm{disc}}$. These are wide simplicial subcategories and $I\subseteq V$. In a hammock marked by $I$, every vertical arrow is an identity, so every row is the same; every leftward column is an identity and disappears in reduction; adjacent rightward columns compose. Thus every reduced hammock is uniquely the repeated single arrow, or the empty path for an identity. In degree $n$ this identifies $H((\mathcal K_*)_n,I_n)(A,B)_n$ with $\mathcal K_*(A,B)_n$. The formulas respect both operators, concatenation and identities, giving an isomorphism $\mathcal K_*\cong\operatorname{diag}H(\mathcal K_*,I)$ by [def-coef-simplicial-hammock-pair]. The ordinary localization of $\pi_0\mathcal K_*$ at identity images is itself. Step 8 says that every vertex of $V$ is already invertible there. Apply [lem-coef-hammock-pi-zero-closure] with $A=\mathcal K_*,U=I,V=W_{\mathcal K}^{\mathrm{disc}}$. It gives local weak equivalences to $H_{\mathcal K}$. Under the displayed isomorphism its functor is precisely $b$, the repeated one-arrow map, so $b$ is locally a weak equivalence. It fixes objects, and therefore is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 4.8, pp.432-433; agent-written specialization and explicit functorial argument, using the existing localization interfaces rather than assuming that pairwise mapping-space identifications preserve composition.

proof.text: Steps 5, 7 and 9 prove the three equivalence assertions for the actual functors whose operator, composition and identity equations were verified in Step 1. The strict square was also proved there on every degree-$r$ arrow, including identity arrows; equality on objects and all simplices is equality of simplicial functors. All constructions stay among the original $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets, and all hammock and coherent diagram categories are small in the enlarged ambient universes stipulated in the statement.
